reviews.title: Verses need context
reviews.body:
I have been using the app for a while.  

 It has helped me to slow down and see how it’s possible to enjoy the bible in a different way by meditating on verses.  I still have my Bible open when I use the app so that I can see the context of the verses and make notes.  I think that is important. 


I have noticed that sometimes the verses picked to meditate on are completely out of context.  When you read the surrounding verses they are not always appropriate to use in the context intended on the app.  That does spoil it for me.  I think the choice of verses used is important.  More consideration should be given to this.    It’s why I have given it only 3 stars as we have to be carefully about bending the word of God into what we want it to mean.

FREE. Im going to keep it plain and simple. This app needs to be FREE and everything within it. And the ads have to go as well. Gods Word and other helpful meditations and such SHOULDN'T have a price tag and be LOCKED if you're not a member. I'm a member of God's Eternal Kingdom and his Word is always open to me NEVER LOCKED.

reviews.title: Illegal charges.

Haven’t even made it to the full 7 days. That isn’t honorable or moral for a “Christian” app. I will never renew my subscription just for that. The app cannot be trusted.

reviews.title: So incredibly didrespectful
reviews.body:
The app gives you an opportunity to set the amount of time you want on your devotional. 5 minutes. 10 minutes. 15 minutes. 20 minutes. Etc.

If you set the app for five minutes, frequently it will go 7 1/2 or eight minutes. It really does not care what you are trying to do and how much time you have. They will go with what they want to do. Kind of like a preacher who runs Long every single Sunday by 20 minutes because “the spirit led him“. That’s great, but this is an app that’s specific to settings for length.

It’s extremely disrespectful to the users time. They can edit it down and do a hard cut off at the designated time. Or at least within 5 to 10 seconds of it.

If you do it daily, this happens at least 3 to 4 days a week, so it’s not an isolated situation.
hard to manage account! I want to cancel auto renew. I have not been able to figure it out! Their directions I found online.Do not work.

Like the program, but not the incessant ask for money!! Follow-up... somebody "responded" to my rating and said "contact us to improve your experience." But, left no way to contact them. I'm a paid subscriber and they still ask for donations constantly.

I immediately uninstalled it when I got to the very end and finally see that you charge something like $39.95 after something like one week. It really tells a lot about who YOU are that you're not willing to tell people up front what they are signing up for before they install the app. Shame on you.

DO NOT DOWNLOAD THIS APP. NOT a pleasant experience. FOR YEARS, I always have my phone on do not disturb at night, with all my volumes off. This app took over my phone volume at full blast and set a secret alarm within the app to go off at sunrise that I didn't set. I had just downloaded it the other day and hadn't had a chance to use it yet. This is NOT a trustworthy app. I finally had to uninstall the app to make an extremely overly loud high pitching chiming alarm that woke up my family. 😡

I'm using the 7 day free trial. That said, I don't have full access. I select something with a lock on it and it wants me to subscribe all over again. So within an hour of doing the free trial I unsubscribed. I'm so glad that there's a free trial because I would feel ripped off. It seems to me, by reading reviews that Abide has questionable practices, my opinion because of the experience.

reviews.title: Can never find topic that is advertised when I click your push notifications
reviews.body:
[Updating a previous very positive review now that my count of devotions heard is up to over 700…(1), I have in 2026 and today still, 4/28/26 been having a  problem a year that an interesting sounding push notification topic  comes up on my iPhone 16e, but when I follow it, it leads to a menu of devotions, and week long study series, —none of which are the subject teased in the notification—Can you have it link directly to the devotion it is advertising? Or at least allow us to search your crammed-full menu? I have a Bible reading plan with my paper Bible I’m lucky to keep up, so I don’t use the “sign up for a week of …” come-ons, really. So my use of the app has fallen significantly though I’m still paying for it, hopefully someone else is gaining satisfaction from the typically well done meditations. Though the breathing and relaxation really doesn’t suit me if I listen in the AM, and I find it all kinda “new age” 

Previous review: Have just lost a paper journal yet again in my house, so the times I’ve “written in my journal” here are also of importance in the wee hours, not bedtime, when I can contemplate & have energy to write at the same time. Have copied some to notes in my iPhone, which I’ve had one of for almost a decade - so maybe more secure than paper? For now anyway. 
(2) Just having listened to the Jenn Stoltzfus / Tyler Bods “I am Loved” devotion, I used it as springboard, with a screenshot of your starry night graphic, on FB; having recalled my Dad using that phrase (1) time to me in my life (we were not a family where “I love you” was said, ever, either: though a good upbringing otherwise.) My suggestion: one problem I have in the Roman’s 8:35-39 journey, which is likely all of our lifetime journals, to see if God ever leaves us, is not the danger / deprivation / illness / storms struggle, nor the power of angels or anything created, except MYSELF. Perhaps it shows narcissism but that scripture leaves put one created thing which I constantly fear WILL show God will or has left me or that I’ve been fooling myself I’m loved: MY OWN FAILURE, amplified by Satan’s semi-true or true accusations… Perhaps a devotion where the pilgrim passes THAT created hurdle would be good. Yeah, I know Paul did address it when he said he was the “chiefest of sinners” but I think we are all, in our failures, and disappointments in ourselves, capable of feeling we are a special case, and even “Chiefer” than Paul… I bet some devotions of this nature will be coming ! You demonstrate God’s power & constancy very well of COURSE. Thanks again

I was looking forward to Christmas and thought surely they’ll have new sleep stories or meditations but no, not a single new sleep story. In fact there hasn’t been more than 3 new sleep stories in MONTHS. What am I even paying $100 a year for at this point? 

The app itself is glitchy. You will see for yourself when you use it. That alone is annoying and not ideal for what’s supposed to be a nice calming app. 

They are constantly peddling various things that of 0 interest to me with no new stories. 

It’s obvious to me that the developers put no effort into this app anymore.

Not worth the money for premium and pointless without paying for premium. Lose-lose situation here.
